tldr: MIND2WEB introduces the first dataset for developing and evaluating generalist web agents that can follow language instructions to complete complex tasks on real-world websites across diverse domains, with over 2,000 tasks from 137 websites spanning 31 domains.
contributions: Introduces MIND2WEB, the first dataset for generalist web agents with diverse domains, real-world websites, and broad interaction patterns
Proposes MINDACT, a two-stage model combining a small LM for candidate element filtering and an LLM for action prediction
Demonstrates that filtering HTML with a small LM significantly improves LLM effectiveness and efficiency for web agent tasks
methods: The authors collected over 2,000 open-ended tasks from 137 websites across 31 domains, with crowdsourced action sequences annotated via Playwright-based tools. They propose MINDACT, a two-stage framework: first, a fine-tuned small cross-encoder LM ranks webpage elements to produce a top-k candidate pool; second, an LLM selects from these candidates using a multi-choice QA formulation and predicts the corresponding action (Click, Type, or Select Option).
results: MINDACT significantly outperforms modeling strategies commonly adopted by prior work. It demonstrates decent generalization to websites and entire domains never seen during training, working with both open-source LLMs (Flan-T5 through fine-tuning) and closed-source LLMs (GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4 through in-context learning). The authors note substantial room for improvement towards truly generalizable agents.
limitations: Raw HTML of real-world websites contains thousands of elements (averaging over 1,000 per page), making direct feeding into LLMs infeasible or cost-prohibitive. While MINDACT shows decent performance, there is still substantial room to improve towards truly generalizable agents. The dataset was limited to US-popular websites across 5 top-level domains.
